ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy SHA 997d9970c437 (deployed 2026-05-05T08:45:37Z) introduced a regression in checkout-service/internal/finalize/order_finalizer.go where the order finalization code iterates over each order_item row and issues a separate SELECT * FROM products WHERE id=$1 query per item (N+1 query pattern). For an order with 12 items this generates 12 individual product lookups per finalization request instead of a single batched query. Under moderate concurrent checkout load this rapidly exhausts the 20-connection PostgreSQL pool, causes query queuing and lock contention on the products table, and results in context deadline exceeded errors and HTTP 500/503 responses to clients.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back checkout-service to the prior stable deploy SHA 5b738e5f6b1b to restore normal DB connection usage and recover the service (ETA < 10 minutes). 2. In the follow-up fix on 997d9970c437, replace the per-item product lookup loop in order_finalizer.go with a single bulk query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = ANY($1) passing the full list of product IDs collected from order_items, reducing N+1 queries to a single round-trip. 3. Optionally, as a defence-in-depth measure, add a covering index on products(id) including price, name, sku to accelerate bulk lookups. 4. Add a slow-query integration test that asserts the number of DB queries issued per order finalization does not exceed a fixed threshold (e.g., 3).
